messages:
maria_support: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — after today's canary rollout of model `llama-2-v1-quant` they report large behaviour changes. Small prompt tweaks now produce completely different outputs (and hallucinations). They say yesterday 'Summarize this:' returned clean bullets, today similar prompt returns unrelated company names. Also seeing a couple of 503s and a p95 latency spike during the rollout window. attaching sample request + ids below. :warning:

maria_support: customer-provided repro (they reproduced this repeatedly):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '
{
  "model": "llama-2-v1-quant",
  "input": "Summarize the following product doc:

- feature A
- feature B

Summary:",
  "max_tokens": 120
}
'

They included two request IDs where behavior diverged: `req_202603041200_az1` and `req_202603041217_bx3`. customer notes that changing the prompt from `Summary:` to `Please summarize:` changes tone and adds hallucinated company names. They tried pinning to `llama-2-v1-fp16` and the issue goes away.

alan_eng: thanks — assigning. were those requests routed through canary? what % rollout did deploy-bot set? also pls paste the exact system prompt + any few-shots the customer used.

maria_support: yes they were on canary. deploy-bot reports canary=10% for the model at 11:58 UTC. system prompt (customer redacted): "You are a concise summarizer." No few-shots. They said payload size ~420 tokens.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout `llama-2-v1-quant` -> started 2026-03-04T11:58:00Z (10% traffic).

shivani_sre: I pulled infra metrics for that window. p95 latency jumped from 180ms -> 720ms for that model pool between 11:58 and 12:05 UTC. Also 503 rate went from 0.02% -> 0.6% (small but customers noticed). CPU on pool nodes spiked and there were a couple of transient OOMs on quantized workers. attaching simplified logs snippet: 

```
[11:58:12Z] pool-node-13: KERNEL_LOAD_WARN quant-kernel fallback -> slower path
[11:59:00Z] pool-node-07: OOM in allocator, retrying request, status=retry
[12:01:40Z] router: 503 -> req=req_202603041217_bx3 route=canary-quant
```

shivani_sre: hypothesis 1) quant kernel fallback + heavier CPU due to different kernel path causing increased latency and some retries -> 503s. hypothesis 2) there's a tokenizer mismatch between fp16 and quant builds (tokenization + padding changed) making some prompt edges parse differently.

alan_eng: good notes. nora, we shipped a tokenizer update in the build that enabled byte-level normalization for some punctuation — could that make tiny prompt punctuation changes hit different tokenization and subsequent positional KV alignment?

nora_engineering: short answer: yes, possible. I ran tokenization diff on "Summarize the following product doc:
Summary:" between `llama-2-v1-fp16` and `llama-2-v1-quant` build and saw different token boundaries when a trailing colon or carriage return present. snippet: 

```
# python pseudo repl
from tokenizer import encode
encode_fp16 = encode("Summarize:\") -> [345, 12, 999]
encode_quant = encode("Summarize:\") -> [345, 12012]
```

nora_engineering: that single merged token in quantized build changes attention offsets for short context prompts — which plausibly explains the style/hallucination shift on minimal edits. we'll need to verify whether the tokenizer table changed or a different tokenizer binary was linked at quant build time.

alan_eng: action items: 1) reproduce locally with exact customer prompt and model binary + tokenizer (maria to share request bodies) 2) if reproducible, rollback canary to 0% for `llama-2-v1-quant` and shift traffic back to `llama-2-v1-fp16` 3) add regression test for tokenization edgecases 4) SRE to check for kernel fallback and OOMs and increase retry/backoff temporarily. who owns rollback?

maria_support: I'll coordinate with customer comms. asking Acme if they want immediate rollback or if they want us to test variants first. they prefer a rollback while we investigate.

kev_product: flagging SLA + account health — AcmeCorp is on an enterprise Dedicated plan; we should proactively offer a postmortem and dedicated point of contact. also capture any billing or quota impacts.

shivani_sre: I'll start rolling some canary traffic off the quant pool. executing controlled drain now.

deploy-bot: Canary update: `llama-2-v1-quant` -> canary=0% (drained) at 2026-03-04T12:03:10Z. routing reverted to `llama-2-v1-fp16`.

maria_support: confirmed with customer — after routing back to `llama-2-v1-fp16` their sample requests match previous behaviour. they want a follow-up postmortem and an ETA for a proper fix.

nora_engineering: I'll start bisecting tokenizer artifacts and run the exact customer prompt across build variants. if tokenizer binary changed we can hotfix by restoring the previous tokenizer mapping in quant build.

alan_eng: also adding a quick test in our rollout gate: when model binary changes, run a tiny suite of prompt-template sensitivity tests (colon, newline, trailing spaces, short system prompts) against a golden baseline before escalating canary > 0%.

maria_support: customer-facing note drafted, will send now: 
> "We've temporarily routed your traffic away from the canary model and confirmed behaviour has reverted. Engineering is investigating root cause; we'll share a timeline for a permanent fix and a postmortem."

kev_product: nice. please include whether this triggered any billing/availability credits. ops, file follow-up for account team.

alan_eng: status — triage done, canary rolled back, SRE monitoring. next: nora to provide root cause or revert plan, alan to add rollout gate test, maria to own customer comms + postmortem. I'll keep this thread updated.

deploy-bot: Post-deploy summary: canary 2026-03-04 11:58 -> 12:03 (10% traffic), rollback executed, no further 503s after 12:05.

maria_support: closing the escalation (customer happy for now). will reopen if we see a recurrence. thanks all. :v:
